papers.title: Monoblock or modular? Impact of stem design and conicity angle on long-term implant survival in revision total hip arthroplasty: a 20-year follow-up registry study on 3647 implants
papers.abstract: Revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) often requires femoral stem revision due to aseptic loosening, instability, or fractures. Long, tapered conical stems are preferred for stability and bone loss management. Recent design changes, like increased conicity angles, aim to enhance fixation and reduce subsidence. Monoblock and modular stems offer distinct pros and cons, but their long-term outcomes remain debated. This study evaluates the long-term survival of monoblock versus modular conical stems, with a focus on conicity angles (2° vs. 3°), using 20 years of registry data. A retrospective review was conducted using the Emilia Romagna Registry of Orthopedic Prosthetic Implants (RIPO) from 2000 to 2021. A total of 3,647 non-cemented conical stems used in rTHA were analyzed: 32.4% monoblock and 67.6% modular. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis assessed implant longevity, stratified by stem design and conicity angle. Use of modular stems increased from 24% to over 83% during the study period. Overall failure rate was 6.3–5.1% for monoblock stems (mainly due to aseptic loosening) and 6.9% for modular stems (primarily due to instability). Monoblock stems had superior 20-year survival (93.7%) compared to modular (86.8%, p = 0.009). Among modular stems, those with 2° conicity had significantly better 15-year survival (91.9%) than 3° designs (88.0%, p = 0.001). No significant difference was observed between conicity angles in monoblock stems. Monoblock stems provide better long-term survival in rTHA. Modular designs, while offering intraoperative flexibility, carry higher revision risk, especially with greater conicity. Stem selection should balance design features with patient needs and surgical expertise.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文为临床登记研究，未涉及增材制造或传统股骨柄的设计、生物力学分析或有限元模拟。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical registry study reporting implant survival rates, with no additive manufacturing, biomechanical modeling, or implant design optimization relevant to the user's direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估翻修全髋关节置换术中，单块与模块化锥形柄及不同锥度角对远期生存率的影响。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析意大利RIPO登记库20年数据，比较3647例非骨水泥锥形柄的生存率。
summary_zh.result: 单块柄20年生存率93.7%优于模块化柄86.8%；模块化柄中2°锥度优于3°。
summary_zh.validation: 基于大型登记数据的Kaplan-Meier生存分析。

summary_en.motivation: To compare long-term survival of monoblock vs modular conical stems and the effect of conicity angles in revision total hip arthroplasty using registry data.
summary_en.method: A retrospective analysis of 3,647 non-cemented conical stems from the RIPO registry (2000–2021) using Kaplan-Meier survival stratified by stem design and conicity angle.
summary_en.result: Monoblock stems showed superior 20-year survival (93.7%) versus modular stems (86.8%); among modular stems, 2° conicity had better survival than 3°.
summary_en.validation: Clinical registry-based survival analysis with 20-year follow-up.

papers.title: Development of a Deep Learning Model for Hip Arthroplasty Templating Using Anteroposterior Hip Radiograph.
papers.abstract: Background: Preoperative templating is an essential step in hip arthroplasty (HA), guiding implant selection and reducing surgical complications. It is typically performed using acetate templates or digital software. These methods, however, depend on the surgeon's experience and may be limited by cost and availability. This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model using plain radiographs to predict implant sizes in HA. Methods: This retrospective study included patients who underwent primary HA using a cementless CORAIL® femoral stem and PINNACLE® acetabular cup. The DL model was trained on 688 preoperative anteroposterior (AP) hip radiographs and validated temporally on 98 additional cases. Implant sizes predicted by the DL model were compared with on-screen templating (acetate templates overlaid on digital images). The actual implanted size was used as the reference standard. Accuracy, mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE) were calculated. Logistic regression was performed to identify factors influencing prediction accuracy. Results: The DL model showed higher accuracy than the on-screen templating for the acetabular cup (88.9% [77.4% to 95.8%] vs. 83.3% [70.7% to 90.2%]) and femoral stem components (85.7% [77.2% to 92.0%] vs. 81.6% [72.5% to 88.7%]), while the on-screen method performed better for the bipolar head (93.2% [81.3% to 98.6%] vs. 72.7% [57.2% to 85.0%]). MAE and RMSE were comparable between the methods for acetabular and femoral stem components (all p > 0.05), with statistically significant differences observed only in the bipolar head (p < 0.01 and 0.02, respectively). Although logistic regression analysis showed trends toward higher accuracy in acetabular size prediction among women and those with shorter height, no demographic factors were statistically significant predictors of accuracy. Conclusions: A DL model using only plain radiographs can accurately predict implant sizes in HA, particularly for the acetabulum and femoral stem. These findings suggest that the DL-based model could be a useful tool in preoperative planning. With further refinement to improve generalizability, this approach could be useful in a routine clinical setting in the future.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address stress shielding, micromotion, bone-implant interface, or additive manufacturing; it is purely a preoperative sizing tool without any biomechanical or mechanical analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 用深度学习从X光片预测髋关节假体尺寸，减少术前规划主观性。
summary_zh.method: 基于688张术前髋关节X光片训练深度学习模型，预测CORAIL股骨柄和PINNACLE髋臼杯尺寸。
summary_zh.result: 模型对髋臼杯和股骨柄尺寸预测准确率分别达88.9%和85.7%，与数字模板法相当或更优。
summary_zh.validation: 用98例独立病例进行时间验证，以实际植入尺寸为金标准比较准确率。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a deep learning model that predicts hip implant sizes from plain radiographs, reducing dependence on surgeon experience and cost.
summary_en.method: A retrospective study using 688 preoperative AP hip radiographs to train a deep learning model for predicting sizes of CORAIL femoral stem and PINNACLE acetabular cup.
summary_en.result: The model achieved accuracy of 88.9% for acetabular cup and 85.7% for femoral stem, comparable or superior to on-screen templating.
summary_en.validation: Temporal validation on 98 cases with actual implanted size as reference, calculating accuracy, MAE, and RMSE.
